content.text: {"grade": 6, "complete": false, "main_gap": "Step 2's justification that some entry >1 always remains rests on a false general principle (a non-increasing positive integer can indeed reach 1); the correct one-line argument (g·ℓ = lcm(m,n) ≥ 2) appears only in the summary, unproved.", "errors": [{"description": "Step 2 asserts that a positive integer sequence that never increases and starts above 1 can never reach 1 — this is plainly false (products can drop to 1 in principle). The true reason, that each move leaves at least one new entry >1 since g·ℓ = lcm(m,n) ≥ 2, is stated only informally in the 'Current best' summary and never justified in the full proof.", "quote": "A positive integer that never increases and starts above 1 can never reach 1; hence\n$P > 1$ after any number of moves."}], "notes": "Termination bound (halving product / non-decreasing count of ones) is correct and clean; the prime-wise gcd-of-valuations invariant and the derivation of the explicit formula for M are fully correct. Only the non-vanishing step is mis-justified, and it is repairable in one line."}
